A 57-year-old female with essential hypertension and type 2 diabetes presents to urgent care with
progressive dyspnea, particularly noticeable during physical exertion such as walking long distances or
climbing stairs. Her medical history includes a 40-year smoking history, and she currently takes
lisinopril, simvastatin, amlodipine, and metformin. She reports no fever, headache, cough, chest pain,
or leg edema. Her vital signs show blood pressure 138/97 mm Hg, heart rate 85/min, respiratory rate
28/min, and temperature 37.0° C (98.7° F). Physical examination reveals expiratory wheezing
throughout all lung fields, bilateral resistance to exhalation in ribs 6-10, and segmental facilitations from
T2-T7. Chest X-ray shows hyperinflated lungs with flattened diaphragms bilaterally. Which of the
following statements accurately describes the patient's condition and appropriate treatment approach?
Answer Choices: (A) The patient has an exhalation rib dysfunction; treatment should be directed to rib
7. (B) The patient has an inhalation rib dysfunction; treatment should be directed to rib 8. (C) The
patient has an inhalation rib dysfunction; treatments should be directed to rib 6. (D) The patient has an
inhalation rib dysfunction; treatment should be directed to rib 7. (E) The patient has an exhalation rib
dysfunction; treatment should be directed to rib 6. (F) The patient has an exhalation rib dysfunction;
treatment should be directed to rib 8. (G) The patient has an exhalation rib dysfunction; treatments
should be directed to ribs 6—10. (H) The patient has hyperinflation-related inhalation restriction;
treatment should focus on rib 6. (I) The patient has an exhalation rib dysfunction; treatment should be
directed to rib 10. (J) The patient has an inhalation rib dysfunction; treatment should be directed to rib

10.
 A. The patient has an exhalation rib dysfunction; treatment should be directed to rib 7.
B. The patient has an inhalation rib dysfunction; treatment should be directed to rib 7.
C. The patient has an exhalation rib dysfunction; treatment should be directed to rib 6.
D. The patient has an inhalation rib dysfunction; treatments should be directed to rib 6.
E. The patient has an exhalation rib dysfunction; treatment should be directed to rib 10.
F. The patient has an exhalation rib dysfunction; treatments should be directed to ribs 6—10.
G. The patient has hyperinflation-related inhalation restriction; treatment should focus on rib 6.
H. The patient has an inhalation rib dysfunction; treatment should be directed to rib 8.
I. The patient has an inhalation rib dysfunction; treatment should be directed to rib 10.
J. The patient has an exhalation rib dysfunction; treatment should be directed to rib 8.
